source_document: Protein-Tool-Evidence-Review (owner, health-tools folder) and DEC-86, approved at HG-02 on 27 Oct 2026
purpose: The primary-source table for TC-FR1-07-AS-08: every BANDS row must lie inside the range of a source it cites (key appears in the row source text). lo/hi are null where the source gives no numeric g/kg range.
ceiling_rationale: The scope of this general tool (DEC-86), not a safety limit; ISSN 2017 allows 2.3-3.1 g/kg only for trained people losing fat.

sources.figure: Safe level 0.83 g/kg; pregnancy +1/+9/+31 g a day by trimester; breastfeeding +19 g (first 6 months), +12.5 g after

sources.population: Men 65+ with functional limitation, no exercise
sources.figure: 1.3 vs 0.8 g/kg for 6 months: no gain in lean mass, strength or function

sources.guideline: Tagawa et al. 2021, dose-response meta-analysis of randomised trials
sources.population: Adults, with or without resistance training
sources.figure: Lean mass rises steeply up to a breakpoint of 1.3 g/kg, then more slowly; the band 1.0-1.4 spans the breakpoint

sources.guideline: AND / Dietitians of Canada / ACSM joint position (2016)
Morton et al. 2018, meta-analysis of 49 randomised trials
Wycherley et al. 2012, meta-analysis of 24 randomised trials
sources.figure: About 1.25 vs 0.72 g/kg: more fat lost and lean mass kept
1.0-1.2 healthy; 1.2-1.5 when active, ill or malnourished

sources.guideline: Nunes et al. 2022, meta-analysis of 74 randomised trials
sources.figure: Lean-mass benefit at 1.2-1.59 g/kg in over-65s who strength-train; 1.6+ under 65
Set individually; about 0.8 g/kg in stages 3-5, not more than 1.3 if progressive (KDIGO); 0.55-0.6 under supervision (KDOQI). The tool gives no number.
